newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House panel action on banking bill postponed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House panel action on banking bill postponed.

text.p: The House Rules Committee's consideration of banking legislation was postponed Tuesday, and banking groups speculated that parts of the bill might end up attached to a stopgap spending measure this week.
The postponement resulted from concern that there was not enough support in the full House to bring the bill to the floor for a vote, Congressional aides and lobbyists said.
Rumors circulated that House Majority Whip Tom DeLay, R-Texas, had conducted an informal count of potential votes, but his spokesman said that was not true.
A House Banking Committee spokesman said the legislation was still "alive," though consideration by the Rules Committee had been postponed.

House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach, R-Iowa, is pushing for passage of banking legislation this session. The bill aims to bolster the undercapitalized thrift deposit insurance fund and reduce regulatory burdens on banks. It also includes some modernization provisions.
"There are a number of different courses of action being considered by Mr. Leach and by the leadership. Discussions are taking place; nothing's been ruled out," the spokesman said.
Banking industry lobbyists speculated that pieces of the bill -- the thrift-fund fix and regulatory relief -- could be attached to a short-term spending bill.
They also said legislation may emerge from the Senate side. A Senate Banking Committee spokesman said the Senate was waiting to see what happened in the House.
A spokesman for the Rules Committee said the panel would meet at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT Wednesday to consider other items, leaving open the possibility it would take up the banking bill at that time.
